4.said: The pre-merge review came back **FAIL**, and it was right. That changed the session materially. ## What the review caught **1. Authorization (critical).** `handler.ts` derives `role` from the **URL path**, which proves nothing about the caller. All roles share one Cognito pool, `/customer/auth/{proxy+}` has no gateway authoriser, and `GetUser` succeeds for any valid token — so reaching `case 'delete-account'` under a `/customer/…` URL only meant the caller *typed* "customer". A vendor or commissioner could have irreversibly deleted their own Cognito login, and because the anonymize lane finds no `customers` row for them it returned `ignored` and my code **deleted the login while erasing nothing**, orphaning their real record. Federated accounts were worse: they skip the password block, so a valid bearer alone sufficed. I verified this myself before acting. The decisive evidence is `register.ts:163-166` — *"Authorization uses Cognito group membership"* — which my handler never consulted. Fixed by resolving the role from the token and failing closed; decoding is sound because `getUser` already made Cognito vouch for that exact string. **2. Stack-trace leak (high).** `aws/CLAUDE.md` p

rulings.what: aws work rides pe/customer-app-ios-release, not the plan's product/customer-account-deletion
rulings.why: the console run's git strategy explicitly overrides Session-budget branch names for every scoped repo; and hetzner/config/aws-pin.sha (56491a3c) == aws origin/main HEAD, so 'off the pin' and 'off the default branch' are the SAME base commit — the pin-delta ship-gate condition is unaffected
rulings.costIfWrong: a reviewer looking for product/customer-account-deletion finds nothing; the PR is on pe/customer-app-ios-release in example-org/aws

rulings.what: ran 'task validate:openapi:redocly:customer' + spectral instead of the plan's 'task validate:openapi:public'
rulings.why: no such task exists in aws/contracts/Taskfile.yml — the verbs are role-scoped (redocly|spectral):(admin|customer|...); 'customer' is the role this change touches, 'public' would not have linted it at all
rulings.costIfWrong: none for this change; the plan's Phase-4 step 5 command name is stale and should be corrected if reused

rulings.what: refreshed BOTH graphs but recorded only hetzner's new counts in docs; left aws's CLAUDE.md + the hub rule's aws row at the 2026-09-03 numbers
rulings.why: aws's graph is local-only/gitignored so the counts describe a machine-local artifact, the hub rule says outright that a stale node count is harmless, and the only way to land the update was a docs-only push that would have restarted a validate-pr run mid-flight on an org whose Actions budget breaker kills the whole fleet's CI. hetzner's refresh DID land because its rule prescribes folding a doc refresh into a change that ships anyway - and the pin-bump PR is exactly that
rulings.costIfWrong: aws/CLAUDE.md and hub .claude/rules/graph-tool.md under-report aws by 33 nodes / 90 edges until the next rebuild; nothing reads these numbers except a human budgeting context

rulings.what: parked the phase on the change window with the aws PR still unmerged, rather than merging aws today and parking after
rulings.why: aws PR #173's test-lambdas check and the independent pre-merge review were both still running when the session's useful work ran out; merging before reading the review would defeat the point of dispatching it, and the hetzner deploy is blocked until Monday either way so nothing is gained by rushing the aws merge
rulings.costIfWrong: Monday's resume does the aws merge as well as the deploy - one extra step in an already-scripted resume; the handoff lists it as step 3

rulings.what: dispatched an independent pre-merge REVIEW mid-build (unrecorded), separate from the plan's formal QA gate, and acted on its findings before merging
rulings.why: the plan's QA step runs at phase-finish, which for this phase is after a production deploy; a review that lands after the merge cannot stop a bad merge. It returned FAIL on two real defects - a URL-path role check that let any role self-delete, and a stack-trace leak - both of which would otherwise have shipped
rulings.costIfWrong: none to the gate: no QA verdict was recorded, the formal sonnet QA subagent is still owed at the true finish and must read the MERGED diff, since this review saw cac6fe38 only and not the d4966b0e fixes
